items.title: Joe Harris Interview, 1961-04-12
items.q: I think Santa Picora and others he knew.

ctx.x: outside? No, I tell you, we picked him up in Monroe, Louisiana. He was traveling with a little band out of Monroe. And the Celestan band was playing at night. They had a club over there on De Hennessy Street, I think it is. He called it the Savoy. Well, this was an opening night that night and we had the job to open it up. That's the time when Anderson was making all those high notes and they wanted to write the ripplet. He was the first to make all those high notes on the trumpets, you know? And that's when we…

The last time I saw the big chief, as they call him, Moore, he was at the famous door. He stopped in to see some of the musicians. I think Santa Picora and others he knew. And I was surprised they all knew him. I'd never known he'd been down this part of the country at that time.

He looked all over town for me. And he found me at the duteron. I was sitting at the boy Drake and I was somebody packing on the show, you know. He was down there with Louis Armstrong. You remember the town of Louis Camp? Yeah, I know. Well, he came down to the duteron. He shook my hand. He played piano too. He did?
